answer: A dynamic bonding curve resists Sybil attacks by enforcing capital requirements that scale with projected trading volume. Each new agent must lock a stake proportional to its expected market impact, raising the cost of flooding the system. As the agent pool grows, the minimum stake climbs, pushing attackers to the summit of financial burden. This creates a high structural dune of locked capital, preventing an attacker from minting sufficient fake agents to manipulate the market over the long horizon.
